headline: The dollar-yen price already jumped on hot inflation news and is stretched at a ceiling; the desk's replays say this bet loses more often than it wins, so wait.

messages.text: I'd skip this one. USD/JPY is at 158.80, right under today's high of 158.85. Buying here is like chasing a bus that already left the stop.
The 1-hour RSI (a gauge of how stretched a move is, over 70 means 'very stretched') reads 76.3. That is the kind of reading where rises often pause or slip back.
The desk replayed this trade 1,500 times. The price hit the target first only about 26% of the time and hit the safety exit first about 67%. On average it lost money.
Real past data agrees: in 59 similar setups, the target came first only 10 times and the stop came first 33 times.
A bank analyst, StoneX, calls this a seven-week 'resistance standoff', meaning sellers have been pushing the price back near this area for weeks. Snippet only, but it fits the chart.
The big reason for the jump, hot US inflation, is already in the price. Another bank, ING, even warns Japan could surprise with good growth, which would hurt USD/JPY.

argument:
The proposed LONG USD/JPY is a late entry after a news-driven spike. At 158.80 the pair sits 0.05 below today's high (158.85) and about 0.94 above today's low (157.86), roughly six 1-hour ATRs of movement already done today (1h ATR 0.16). The 1h RSI is 76.3 and the 15m RSI 70.7, both overbought; the 15m and 5m MACD histograms are negative (-0.006 and -0.009), a sign that upward momentum is already fading on shorter timeframes.

The code-checked optimizer returned NO_EDGE: no plan passed the odds test. The best plan (entry 158.80, stop 158.64 = 1x ATR, target 159.12 = 2R) reaches target first 26.5% of replays versus stop first 66.6%, with an average of -0.099R; real history over 59 samples gave 10 targets, 33 stops, 16 neither. A 2R trade needs roughly 33% wins to break even, so this is clearly below that.

Context: StoneX describes a seven-week resistance standoff near this level (snippet only). The hot US CPI, hawkish Waller comments and rate-hike bets (FXStreet) pushed the dollar up broadly today (dollar index +0.7%, US 10-year yield 5.015%, +3.1%), but that news is already reflected in the price, and the context desk rates the backdrop only NEUTRAL, not a tailwind. ING flags a Japanese growth surprise as a risk to USD/JPY. The event guard is CLEAR, so no scheduled shock helps either side; with nothing fresh to push price through the ceiling, mean reversion after a stretched spike is the more likely path.

evidence.claim: USD/JPY 158.80; 1h RSI 76.3, 15m RSI 70.7; day high 158.85, day low 157.86
evidence.plain: Price is stretched and sitting right at today's top after a big climb.

evidence.claim: Optimizer NO_EDGE: target first 26.5%, stop first 66.6%, avg -0.099R; history 10 targets vs 33 stops in 59
evidence.plain: In replays, this trade loses more often than it wins and loses money on average.

evidence.claim: Dollar index +0.7% today, US 10-year yield 5.015% (+3.1%); context verdict NEUTRAL
evidence.plain: The dollar already jumped today, and the wider market is only mixed, not clearly supportive.

evidence.claim: StoneX: 'USD/JPY Seven-Week Resistance Standoff Faces Fed, BoJ'
evidence.plain: Sellers have held the price back near this zone for about seven weeks.

evidence.claim: ING: Japan could deliver a positive growth surprise that would weigh on USD/JPY
evidence.plain: A good Japanese data surprise could push the yen up, which would hurt this trade.

evidence.claim: Hot US CPI puts a 50 bp Fed hike in play; dollar up vs GBP, EUR, AUD, CAD
evidence.plain: The big dollar jump came from inflation news that came out hours ago; it is already in the price.
On the short charts, the upward push is already weakening.

plan_flaws: Optimizer NO_EDGE: best plan reaches target first 26.5% vs stop first 66.6%, avg -0.099R
A 1x ATR stop (about 0.16 on the 1h) is a normal-sized wiggle; 2R target at about 159.12 needs a clean break past 158.85 high and the 7-week ceiling
Entry at the live price is 0.05 below today's high with 1h RSI 76.3, a stretched entry
Only one known level (today's high 158.85) lies above; no support-based reason for upside beyond it in levels.json
plan_flaws_plain: The desk's replays say this trade loses more often than it wins.
The safety exit is only a normal-sized wiggle away, so ordinary movement could knock the trade out.
You would be buying right after a big jump, near the top of the day.
The target needs the price to break through a ceiling that has held for weeks.
conditions_to_reconsider: Only if price pulls back to a lower area and holds, or closes an hour clearly above today's high of 158.85 and stays there, and the desk's optimizer finds a plan that passes the odds test.
